hints.title: Parameterized Rank Offset Extraction
hints.text: Extracting the n-th distinct pay grade requires skipping preceding top values and handling tables with insufficient distinct records.

hints.title: Zero-Based Offset Calculation
hints.text: The n-th largest distinct value corresponds to a zero-based offset of n minus one. Sorting unique amounts in descending order isolates the candidate.

hints.title: Function Definition Blueprint
hints.text: In MySQL, declare n = n - 1. Return scalar query: select distinct salary from Employee order by salary desc limit 1 offset n.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
CREATE FUNCTION getNthHighestSalary(N INT) RETURNS INT
BEGIN
SET N = N - 1;
  RETURN (
      SELECT DISTINCT salary
      FROM Employee
      ORDER BY salary DESC
      LIMIT 1 OFFSET N
  );
END
```

variables: N: number of records in Employee table
complexity.notes: Distinct sort with single row offset fetch.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Dense rank window queries without scalar encapsulation return empty result sets rather than null when n exceeds available distinct salaries.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Scalar subquery wrapping limit offset returns null automatically when no matching row exists.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correct zero-based index adjustment (N = N - 1) and distinct deduplication before ordering.
